rationale_evidence.anchor: Rationalism is a long-standing philosophical school that can be characterized as an attempt to extend the perceived methodology of mathematics to all of knowledge. ... The main opposition to rationalism is empiricism, the view that sense experience, and not pure reason, is the source of knowledge. ... mathematical knowledge seems to be based on proof, not observation, mathematics is an apparent counterexample to the main empiricist thesis. Indeed, mathematics is sometimes held up as a paradigm of a priori knowledge.
rationale_evidence.statement: Frames Chapter 1's opening problem: rationalism attempts to extend mathematics' perceived methodology (proof, pure reason) to all of knowledge (Descartes, Spinoza, Leibniz), while empiricism holds sense experience, not pure reason, is the source of knowledge (Locke, Berkeley, Hume, Mill, later logical positivists); mathematics is an apparent counterexample to empiricism since mathematical knowledge seems based on proof rather than observation, making it a paradigm case of a priori knowledge (knowledge prior to and independent of experience) that empiricists have historically struggled to accommodate.

rationale_evidence.anchor: There are several reasons for the connection between mathematics and philosophy. Both are among the first intellectual attempts to understand the world around us ... mathematics is an important case study for the philosopher. Many issues on the agenda of contemporary philosophy have remarkably clean formulations when focused on mathematics. ... A third reason ... lies in epistemology ... mathematics is a primary tool in our best efforts to understand the world. ... Galileo wrote that the book of nature is written in the language of mathematics. This insightful, enigmatic metaphor highlights the place of mathematics in the scientific/philosophical enterprise of understanding the world, but it does not even hint at a solution of the problem.
rationale_evidence.statement: Gives three reasons for the mathematics-philosophy connection: (1) both fields share ancient shared origins and undergo definitional transformations over what counts as each discipline; (2) mathematics is a clean case study for general philosophical questions of reference (what does a term stand for/represent?) and normativity (what obligates correct reasoning?), since mathematics and logic provide simple, well-formulated cases; (3) mathematics is epistemologically central because it is a primary tool for scientific understanding of the physical, human, and social world -- quoting Galileo's 'the book of nature is written in the language of mathematics' as an insightful but unsolved metaphor for why mathematics plays this role.

rationale_evidence.statement: The philosophically-proposed minimal kernel algebra Omega_K={Discriminate,Qualify,Transition} (from S2219, the kernel-definition-from-evidence-maths-DDD file) maps exactly onto the formal lane's independently-established blockers: Discriminate = the equality/distinguishability relation equiv (the unique minimal cycle cut per Steps 289/291, unique over both graph universes); Qualify = the corpus's own Qualify:Observation x Policy -> Evidence, i.e. G1, named/typed/no body, irreducible; Transition = K_t --delta--> K_{t+1}, i.e. delta, commit case unspecifiable, executed as K1 is K0. This is a genuine independent arrival (derived from 'what must a kernel be able to do', not from the dependency graph, 261.23, or the G1 register) but a NEGATIVE convergence: it solves none of the three, and is a restatement of the blocker set, not a kernel. Registered as new gap G-90 (derived, raises confidence, closes nothing). Sharp consequence stated: any minimal kernel algebra containing Qualify inherits G1 -- since Qualify is the one irreducible gap, a genuinely minimal kernel cannot be closed without closing G1.

Conclusion: a correctly-shaped triple whose three components are exactly the three open items -- a well-posed problem statement, not progress toward closure; must not be mistaken for populating the kernel (per 291's 'shape -> content requires a derivation, and none exists').

rationale_evidence.anchor: Knowledge quantity \neq Knowledge quality ... Purification \neq accumulation
rationale_evidence.statement: Refines purification: P:Sigma_t->Sigma_{t+1} must not assume P(Sigma_t)>Sigma_t (per Step 287's finding that axes lack fully declared orders); instead a desired property Q(Sigma_{t+1})>=Q(Sigma_t) is wanted where Q is a future epistemic-quality functional that does not yet exist (an important research gap). Illustrates via example that K_1={1000 unsupported claims} could contain more information than K_2={100 well-supported claims} yet K_2 may be epistemically superior -- so Knowledge quantity != Knowledge quality, and Purification != accumulation; the kernel should maximize epistemic adequacy, not raw knowledge.
